section_1_overview.objective: Create a transformation-style UGC video that drives purchases by showing the convenience of the PowerBand Resistance Set for busy people who can't always get to the gym.

performance_benchmark.key_winning_element: Visual transformation from frustrated gym-packer to happy portable-fitness user

creator_requirements.demographics: 25-40, any gender, fitness-interested appearance (doesn't need to be a fitness influencer)
creator_requirements.vibe: Relatable, approachable, 'everyday person' energy - NOT fitness model/influencer energy
creator_requirements.setting: Home environment (bedroom, living room, or hotel room for travel angle)
creator_requirements.product_interaction: Actually use the resistance bands, show the quick-change clips, demonstrate portability

opening_options.script: *Looking frustrated at gym bag* 'I used to spend 30 minutes just packing for the gym...'
opening_options.visual: Creator looking annoyed, surrounded by gym equipment/bag

opening_options.script: *Holding up stuffed gym bag* 'There's no way I'm lugging this to my hotel room again.'
opening_options.visual: Show overstuffed gym bag, exasperated expression

opening_options.script: *In a small space, maybe hotel room* 'My gym membership is $80/month and I've gone twice.'
opening_options.visual: Creator in relatable setting, slightly self-deprecating tone

section_2_hook.visual_requirement: Show the 'before' state - frustration, inconvenience, or wasted money on traditional gym approach
do_not: Start with the product in hand (save the reveal)
Open with a generic greeting ('Hey guys!')
section_2_hook.why_this_hook: Transformation hooks achieved 45% hook rate - highest among all tested hook types. The frustrated-to-happy arc creates emotional engagement that carries through the video.

key_messages: The PowerBand set replaces an entire gym's worth of equipment
It's so portable it fits in any bag - laptop bag, carry-on, purse
The quick-change clips make switching resistance levels instant (this is the USP)
talking_points: Show the before frustration transition to 'Then I found these...'
'Five resistance levels in one set - I can do literally every exercise'
'Look how small this packs down' *demonstrate fitting in bag*
'These clips though - I can switch resistance in like 2 seconds' *demonstrate quick-change clips*
'I've done more workouts in my living room this month than I did at the gym all year'

product_showcase_moments.what_to_show: Reveal the product - first view should emphasize how compact/portable
Quick montage of 2-3 exercises OR fit-in-bag moment

section_3_body.tone_guidance: Start with relatable frustration, transition to genuine excitement/relief when showing product. NOT infomercial energy. Think 'telling your friend about something you actually love.'
section_3_body.authenticity_notes: The transition from frustrated to happy should feel earned. Don't oversell - understatement is more credible. The 'this actually changed my routine' angle is more believable than 'THIS CHANGED MY LIFE.'

verbal_cta.primary: 'They're doing 20% off right now with code FIT20 - link's in my bio'
verbal_cta.alternative: 'Link below - use code FIT20 for 20% off and free shipping'

section_4_cta.visual_cta: Product in hand or in use, happy expression, can point down/gesture to link
section_4_cta.offer_to_mention: 20% off with code FIT20 + free shipping
do_not: Sound like you're reading a script
Forget the code - FIT20 must be mentioned verbally

filming.lighting: Natural light preferred, ring light acceptable
filming.background: Home environment - bedroom, living room, or hotel room (avoid gym settings)
filming.audio: Built-in phone mic OK if quiet environment, external mic preferred

versions_needed.note: Same body/CTA, different hook openings (Options A, B, C)

dos: Show genuine frustration → relief emotional arc
Actually demonstrate the quick-change clips (key differentiator)
Film in a relatable home setting
Speak naturally - improvise within the key messages
Show the product fitting into a everyday bag (laptop bag, purse, carry-on)
Include #ad disclosure (beginning or end of video)
donts: Make weight loss claims or promises
Compare to specific gym brands by name
Film in a gym (defeats the message)

compliance.claim_restrictions: No weight loss claims, no 'guaranteed' language, no specific competitor mentions

top_performer_to_emulate.reference: UGC_BeforeAfter_Mike_V2 (will be provided as video file)

why_it_works.hook: Opens with relatable frustration (packing gym bag), immediately creates 'same!' moment with viewer
why_it_works.body: Shows the transformation naturally - not forced. Product feels like a genuine discovery.
why_it_works.cta: Casual recommendation, not hard sell. Code mentioned clearly but not screamed.

elements_to_borrow: Showing the product fitting in a normal bag (not a fitness bag)
The 'wait, this actually works?' genuine reaction
Mentioning specific use case (travel, home, hotel)

issues: Obvious gym setting defeats convenience message
Not showing the actual USP (quick-change clips)

hook_options: A: *Frustrated at gym bag* 'I used to spend 30 minutes just packing for the gym...'
B: *Holding stuffed bag* 'There's no way I'm lugging this to my hotel room again.'
C: *Small space* 'My gym membership is $80/month and I've gone twice.'
quick_reference_card.cta: '20% off with code FIT20 - link in bio'
quick_reference_card.must_include: #ad disclosure, code FIT20, quick-change clip demo
quick_reference_card.must_avoid: Weight loss claims, gym settings, competitor names

body_checklist.item: Product shown fitting in everyday bag

expected_performance.rationale: Replicating proven winner with same hook type, structure, and tone. New creator may not match exactly but should be within 20% of original.

key_success_factors: Hook nails the frustrated → relieved transition
Quick-change clips get clear demo (USP visibility)
Creator is relatable, not fitness-influencer polished
potential_failure_points: Too short - doesn't give enough time for transformation arc
